title: As group size increases, individuals modify their vocal features to signal cooperation while remaining recognizable
why_promising: Primary Bernese Swiss German interactive-game speech; MAUS segmentation and labeling were manually checked/corrected in Praat; 749 phonologically annotated word signals before outlier removal; supplied/analyzed production measures include harmonicity, jitter, F0, formant dispersion, and duration.
open_question: Locate authoritative public repository/supplement containing token-level measurements and/or corrected annotations; verify license and whether all analyzed word signals and original acoustic variables are downloadable before core admission.

title: Revisiting glottalic production mechanisms: evidence from phonological and non-phonological ejectives in real-time MRI
why_promising: Primary Amharic and British English rt-MRI production; acoustic waveform/spectrogram inspected manually in Praat; intervals include closure, burst, post-burst lag, following vowel, with target-stop closure used for articulatory analysis; English ejective realizations additionally categorized auditorily.
open_question: Find a public data deposit for manual segmentation, acoustic measurements, MRI-derived articulatory contours and participant/token metadata; thesis alone establishes provenance but not public observation-level availability.

title: A semi-automatic pipeline for transcribing and segmenting child speech
why_promising: Primary field recordings from 275 Scottish-English-speaking children; study explicitly compares automated outputs with manually annotated reference data and uses manual transcription correction in the pipeline, making the human reference subset potentially admissible.
open_question: Locate project repository/deposit and isolate the fully manually annotated reference observations from merely automatically aligned material; verify token counts, vowel measures, file lineage, and redistribution/license before admission.
